comparisons.peer_summary: Prior to adopting the new accounting standard on January 1, 2023, the Corporation accounted for modifications of loans to borrowers experiencing financial difficulty as Troubled Debt Restructurings (TDRs) only when the modification resulted in a concession.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and BAC disclose their historical accounting treatment for credit card loan modifications prior to the January 1, 2023 standard adoption, defining these concessions as Troubled Debt Restructurings (TDRs). JPM specifies that these modifications generally involved fixed 60-month payment plans with reduced interest rates, whereas BAC provides the broader accounting criterion that concessions were reported as TDRs only when the modification resulted in a concession, without detailing the specific plan terms in this disclosure segment.

sentences.text: For periods ending prior to January 1, 2023, modifications of credit card loans where the Firm granted concessions to borrowers who were experiencing financial difficulty were generally accounted for and reported as TDRs.
These concessions involved placing the customer's credit card account on a fixed payment plan, generally for 60 months, and typically included reducing the interest rate on the credit card account.

Prior to adopting the new accounting standard on loan modifications, the Corporation accounted for modifications of loans to borrowers experiencing financial difficulty as TDRs, when the modification resulted in a concession.

comparisons.peer_summary: Citi offers long-term loan modification programs for credit card borrowers experiencing financial difficulty, typically involving interest rate reductions, fixed payment plans of up to 60 months, and cancellation of the available line of credit.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and Citi disclose specific operational details of long-term loan modification programs for financially distressed credit card borrowers, specifically noting the use of fixed payment plans capped at 60 months and interest rate reductions. JPM notes that these concessions were historically reported as TDRs, while Citi focuses on the program mechanics (including line of credit cancellation) and does not link these specific terms to TDR accounting in this text, as Citi also notes a switch to a new accounting policy in 2023.

comparisons.peer_summary: The firm may modify terms for borrowers in financial difficulty, primarily via term extensions; modified loans were mostly performing, with negligible defaults in 2024 and ~$100 million charged off in 2023 from previously modified loans.
comparisons.comparison: While both JPM and GS discuss modifications for borrowers in financial difficulty, the nature of the modifications and accounting treatment differ. JPM's disclosure focuses on the historical TDR accounting framework for fixed-rate, 60-month credit card plans prior to 2023. In contrast, GS discloses that its modifications (which include corporate, CRE, and credit card loans) were primarily term extensions rather than fixed-rate payment plans, and does not reference TDR accounting in this context, reflecting the post-2023 standard environment.
